expectations.text: Gives three completeness gates checkable before the first session and free of any threshold to argue about.
Gate: every concurrent session has a named moderator, or the interaction surface for it is closed.
expectations.evidence: 'If no one is named, we close the chat for that session.'

expectations.text: States that gate requires a name, not a function or a role.
Gate: every speaker has joined the platform the event actually runs on at least once before the day.
Gate: the fallback line is published, and the person who will say it out loud knows the sentence.
Labels every remaining metric as self-set rather than an industry standard, and says so when presenting it.
expectations.evidence: 'Every number below is a commitment we choose. None is an industry standard'.

expectations.text: Does not invent an industry benchmark, published target percentage, or external standard to hit.
expectations.evidence: 'I will not invent a show-up rate'; the skill gives no benchmark.

expectations.text: Offers sessions delivered without an audience-visible failure over sessions scheduled.
States that a session which ran with no audio counts as a failure.
expectations.evidence: 'A session with no audio counts as a failure.'

expectations.text: Offers time from a feed dropping to the audience being told something.
Offers questions relayed to a speaker against questions asked, as the measure of whether moderation staffing was real or nominal.
expectations.evidence: KPI 4, 'whether the moderation was real or nominal'.

expectations.text: Offers speakers who joined a check before the day over speakers scheduled, as the one leading indicator available before anything goes wrong.
Recommends picking two or three, writing down what change each would trigger, and recording them before the event rather than after.
expectations.evidence: 'Record the three committed KPIs, and the action each one triggers, before the event, not after.'
